page: Microsoft Azure D32lds_v6 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor. Operating under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, it features 32 virtual CPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU runs at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and is equipped with 260 MB of L3 cache. The system is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core.

This server includes 1890 GB of local storage and supports Premium Storage. The Intel Xeon processor includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, including VNNI and BF16, and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions, specifically AMX_TILE and AMX_INT8. These hardware features accelerate vector and matrix operations, which are beneficial for mathematical computations and cryptography tasks supported by integrated AES and SHA extensions.

Benchmarks indicate strong memory bandwidth for large block operations, with read speeds reaching 211.12 GB/sec and write speeds at 102.72 GB/sec. Single-threaded gzip compression and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression also demonstrate strong performance. In Geekbench tests, the server shows strong single-core and multi-core capabilities, with top-tier performance in image processing. For language model tasks, it achieves top-tier text generation speeds of 396.8 tokens/sec on small 135M models, though performance drops to a weak 2.77 tokens/sec for large 70B models. Given the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and local storage, this instance is suited for compute-intensive workloads, web serving, image processing, and database operations that do not require high memory-to-CPU ratios.
description: Microsoft Azure D32lds_v6 is a compute-focused x86_64 server featuring a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor with 32 vCPUs, 16 physical cores, and a 4.2 GHz clock speed. It is configured with 64.0 GB of memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per core ratio, and includes 1890 GB of local storage with Premium Storage capabilities. The processor supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX, which enhance vector and matrix calculations. Benchmark results show strong performance in large-block memory bandwidth, image processing, and small-model LLM inference, alongside average database and compilation speeds. This server is optimized for compute-heavy workloads, static web serving, and localized database operations where high CPU performance is required but memory demands are moderate.
